name: Urban Waterfront Spaces: Water-Friendly Preference and Emotions (Min River, Fuzhou)
description: Faithful replication of Yan et al. (2024), Forests 15:25, "How Do Urban Waterfront Landscape Characteristics Influence People's Emotional Benefits? Mediating Effects of Water-Friendly Environmental Preferences". Each participant is assigned one of 42 waterfront spaces along the Min River in Fuzhou, China: 14 blue-dominated (B01–B14), 14 co-dominated (C01–C14) and 14 green-dominated (G01–G14). The space type is drawn at random, then one of its sites. They look around the site's panoramic photograph for 5 minutes. Then they rate the place on the 18-item Water-friendly Environmental Preferences Scale (coherence, legibility, complexity, mystery, biophilia, attachment; 1–5) and report their current emotions on the 20-item PANAS (1–5). The 42 panoramas are the paper's own photographs, cropped from Figures 2–4 (CC BY 4.0). They are used with credit and the template is taken down if the authors object. Differences from the original study: (1) the paper projected the panoramas on a large screen in a lab and recorded skin conductance; here the panorama is shown in the browser and scrolled sideways, with no physiological measures. (2) The figures print the panoramas at about 1015 × 245 px, smaller than the originals. (3) The paper does not say how sites were assigned to participants; the template gives each participant one random site, balanced over the three space types. (4) The PANAS words are shown in the standard PANAS order with the standard 1–5 anchors; the paper lists them by dimension and only says a 5-point Likert scale. (5) The site indicators (green and blue visibility from image segmentation; naturalness, water-friendliness, openness and cleanliness from 50 experts) are not part of the participant survey. (6) The paper recruited 150 university students; the template asks for gender, age and study level and is open to anyone.
author: Yan, Chen; Cai, Xiangwu; Wu, Yuping; Tang, Xuehong; Zhou, Yuxuan; Yang, Qin; Li, Fangying; Lan, Siren; Lin, Li

elements.title: Water-friendly Environmental Preferences Scale (WEPS)
elements.description: Same site key. Value: {coh1..att3}, 18 items, 1 = strongly disagree … 5 = strongly agree. Dimension score = mean of its three items (coherence, legibility, complexity, mystery, biophilia, attachment).

elements.name: panas
elements.title: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS), right now
elements.description: Same site key. Value: 20 emotion words, 1 = very slightly or not at all … 5 = extremely. PA = mean of the 10 positive words, NA = mean of the 10 negative words. Analysis as in the paper: ANOVA of WEPS dimensions, PA and NA across space types (BDS, CDS, GDS); correlate with the site indicators; mediation WLC → WEP → EB.
